claim: arch_changeset_builder.md:87, the Cleanup op shape table: `deps | none — the finished task the cleanup follows is not named; the journal's removed event is the tie`. Its premise is stated in arch_action_classifier.md:12: `an absent task means the code already shipped, so the repository now holds code answering to no spec node and a cleanup task is created to have it deleted`. Both hold only when nothing live still calls the removed node's code.
authoritative_source: spec/proposals/2026-08-31-task-lifecycle.md:39 defines component renames as delete+create (`BeadReader` -> `TaskReader`), and :59 prices that as `an old-node close and a new create in the mint`. In a rename the deleted half's code is not dead: a live node keeps calling it until the created half and the caller's own change land. The undecided case: what a cleanup task depends on, and what its terminal state is, when the code it must delete is still called by a node whose task is open.
evidence: Bead spexmachina-swvx.7 (`Code cleanup: plan/BeadReader`), PR #467. `cmd/spex/plan.go:107` still calls `plan.ReadBeadsBytes`; the created half `spexmachina-swvx.14` (TaskReader) and the caller's bead `spexmachina-swvx.21` (PlanCommand, owner of `--beads`) are both open. Because the cleanup op was minted with `deps: none`, `br ready` listed swvx.7 before either, and deleting `plan/bead_reader.go` breaks `go build ./...`. The bead has no legal outcome under the current leaves: not implementable (the deletion needs swvx.21's code, out of scope), not a spec defect the implementer could name in its own contract, not approvable (a PR carrying only a `blocks` edge would close the only bead tracking the deletion). Five review rounds in faber run 20260903-114514 restated that and the loop exhausted; the edge `swvx.7 blocks-on swvx.21` had to be added by hand.
proposed_fix: Order cleanups after the implementation they trail, using inputs the plan already reads. (1) arch_changeset_builder.md Cleanup op shape, `deps`: the frontier of the batch — every non-cleanup create and retarget op that no other op in the batch depends on — as `ref:op`, plus every task the task-state document lists as in flight, as `ref:task`. The closure of those deps is every non-cleanup task of the epic (epics run one at a time), so the cleanup becomes ready exactly when the last of them closes, with a minimal edge set; the journal's `removed` event stays the tie. (2) arch_topological_sorter.md:9, type tier: add a fourth tier, cleanups, after test tasks, so every `ref:op` a cleanup names is in the adapter's substitution table before the adapter reaches it. (3) arch_action_classifier.md:12: `code answering to no spec node` -> `code answering to no spec node, or to a removed half of a rename whose successor and callers have not yet landed`. The alternative considered: exact deps on the removed node's former users, read from the pre-change graph via a new `used_by` field `spex diff` would emit. Rejected here because it adds an input and a format version and under-waits when a caller's `uses` edge was never declared; the frontier rule can only over-wait. Out of scope: whether data_flow tasks should precede all implementation, and whether the tier order belongs in the profile — neither is stated in the spec today, so both are proposal material, not drift.
